meta.name: Sovereign IQ
meta.disclaimer: This executive diagnostic provides directional technical sovereignty and regulatory defensibility analysis. It does not constitute legal counsel.

pillars.name: Data Sovereignty & Localization
pillars.desc: Data at rest, in transit, and in-memory residency across borders.

pillars.name: Jurisdictional Reach & Extraterritoriality
pillars.desc: Immunity to foreign subpoenas, CLOUD Act reach & conflict of laws.

pillars.name: Operational & Personnel Sovereignty
pillars.desc: Local clearance, 24/7 follow-the-sun admin bounds & out-of-band telemetry.

pillars.name: Cryptographic & Technical Autonomy
pillars.desc: HYOK/External Key Management, HSM isolation & Confidential Computing.

pillars.name: Software, Vendor & Supply Chain Sovereignty
pillars.desc: CTPP concentration, exitability, open standards & hardware provenance.

maturityStages.label: Reactive
maturityStages.desc: Compliance handled ad-hoc and after the fact; cross-border and foreign access exposure largely unmapped.

maturityStages.label: Aware
maturityStages.desc: Obligations identified; residency addressed on paper but operational and jurisdictional controls patchy.

maturityStages.label: Structured
maturityStages.desc: Defined policies and ownership; residency localized, but vendor-held encryption keys and SaaS blindspots remain.

maturityStages.label: Managed
maturityStages.desc: Controls tested and evidenced; HYOK/BYOK deployed, sub-processor chains audited, and exit strategies documented.

maturityStages.label: Sovereign-by-Design
maturityStages.desc: Sovereignty embedded in architecture, procurement & CI/CD; provably immune to extraterritorial overreach.

sections.name: Jurisdictional Exposure
sections.desc: US parent reach, CLOUD Act & TIAs

bfsi.name: Tier-1 Global BFSI & Banking
bfsi.narrative: Global BFSI peers demonstrate high data localization (P1: 75), but face acute compliance pressure under DORA Art. 28 and APRA CPS 230 for single-cloud concentration (P5: 60).

healthcare.name: Global Healthcare & BioPharma
healthcare.narrative: Pharma leads in physical clinical data residency (P1: 82), but faces high exposure to US cloud providers for AI analytics and genomics pipelines.

public_sector.name: Public Sector & Sovereign Gov
public_sector.narrative: Government estates exhibit strict localization and domestic support clearance, with rising adoption of SecNumCloud and dedicated sovereign cloud enclaves.

fintech_payments.name: APAC & Challenger FinTech
fintech_payments.narrative: Fast-growth FinTechs excel in container portability and agile infrastructure, but struggle with CTPP concentration on single public clouds.

cross_industry.name: Global Multi-Enterprise Baseline
cross_industry.narrative: Cross-industry enterprise baseline reflects legacy hybrid setups with nascent sovereignty governance and unmapped SaaS dependencies.

questions.q: How is your operating technology estate distributed across delivery archetypes?
questions.hint: Digital sovereignty spans the entire estate — from on-prem DCs to hyperscale cloud and SaaS.

opts.text: Public Cloud IaaS & PaaS (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle Cloud, Alibaba, OVH)
On-Premises Data Centers & Private Colocation (Equinix, owned facilities, mainframes)
Enterprise SaaS (Microsoft 365, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Workday, Snowflake, SAP)
AI & Large Language Models (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, self-hosted LLMs, agentic AI)
Edge, Industrial SCADA & Remote Branch Infrastructures

questions.q: What percentage of your production core / mission-critical workloads run on public cloud vs on-prem / SaaS?
questions.hint: Slide to estimate public cloud proportion. 0% = Pure On-Prem; 100% = All-in Public Cloud.

questions.q: Do you utilize Artificial Intelligence or automated decision models for customer-facing or regulated functions?
questions.hint: Engages EU AI Act, UK AI Principles, and sector-specific model governance rules.

opts.text: Yes — High-impact AI (credit scoring, insurance underwriting, biometrics, hiring, health diagnosis)
Yes — Operational AI (fraud detection, chatbots, code assistance, internal process automation)
Yes — Foundation Model Provider / Fine-tuner (pre-training or fine-tuning GPAI models)
No — AI is currently restricted or in non-production sandbox only

questions.q: What categories of sensitive or regulated data do you store, process, or transmit?
questions.hint: Special categories trigger strict statutory transfer barriers and domestic localization mandates.

opts.text: Citizen / Customer Financial Records (account balances, transactions, payment cards)
Special-Category Personal Data (biometrics, health, genetic, government IDs, facial scans)
National Security, Defense, or Critical Infrastructure SCADA telemetry
Standard Commercial B2B data & corporate business records

questions.q: Where is your primary production data physically stored and hosted at rest?
questions.hint: Local physical residency is the foundational prerequisite — though not the only requirement.

opts.text: 100% within the domestic border of operating country (e.g. within KSA, UAE, or strictly in EU/UK)
Mixed: Primary data in-country, but analytical data or archives stored in foreign regions
Global Multi-Tenant Cloud: Hosted wherever the hyperscaler routes the regional cluster

questions.q: Where do your database snapshots, disaster recovery targets, and backup archives reside?
questions.hint: A common audit failure: domestic primary storage with cross-border automated backup replication.

opts.text: Strictly in-country / domestic dedicated secondary zone
Cross-border secondary region within the same economic bloc (e.g. Frankfurt -> Dublin in EEA)
Cross-border to US, APAC, or global backup pools without contractual isolation

questions.q: What is the corporate parent headquarters jurisdiction of your primary hyperscalers and SaaS providers?
questions.hint: Under the US CLOUD Act, a US-headquartered parent must comply with US warrants regardless of where data sits.

opts.text: Primarily US-headquartered providers (AWS, Microsoft, Google Cloud, Salesforce, Oracle, Snowflake)
Mix of US hyperscalers with certified local sovereign partners (e.g. T-Systems, Thales, stc, e&)
Strictly domestic / national sovereign cloud providers (OVHcloud, Hetzner, domestic telecom clouds)

questions.q: What contractual vehicle governs your relationship with cloud and technology providers?
questions.hint: Contracting directly with a US parent entity waives corporate veil protections vs contracting with an EU/local entity.

opts.text: Direct contract with local/in-country operating subsidiary governed exclusively by local law
Standard global terms governed by Delaware, California, or non-domestic foreign courts
Contract terms unexamined / default click-through enterprise agreement

questions.q: Have you conducted Transfer Impact Assessments (TIAs) covering foreign lawful access (CLOUD Act, FISA 702)?
questions.hint: Required by EDPB Schrems II guidance, UK ICO, and KSA PDPL before cross-border routing.

opts.text: Yes — Formal TIAs executed and regularly reviewed with documented supplementary technical measures
Partially — Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) signed, but formal surveillance analysis incomplete
No — Relying solely on provider marketing claims and standard Data Processing Addenda (DPAs)

questions.q: How is administrative support and root-level infrastructure maintenance handled by your technology providers?
questions.hint: Follow-the-Sun models allow engineers in India, the US, or Eastern Europe to hold elevated access to live estates.

opts.text: Strictly bounded: 24/7 support operated exclusively by cleared domestic/EU nationals in-country
Customer Approval Required: Provider support requires Just-In-Time (JIT) customer approval and access broker logging
Standard Follow-the-Sun: Global support engineers access environments based on timezone rotations

questions.q: For on-premises hardware, storage, and firewalls, are remote out-of-band management channels (iDRAC/iLO) active?
questions.hint: Hardware vendor call-home telemetry and remote support tunnels represent unmapped extraterritorial vectors.

opts.text: Air-gapped / Strictly internal OOB networks with all vendor phone-home telemetry blocked
Connected OOB networks with automated vendor telemetry and remote diagnostics enabled
No on-premises infrastructure / Pure Cloud

questions.q: In SaaS applications (M365, Salesforce, ServiceNow), does the SaaS provider hold administrative access to tenant data?
questions.hint: Most enterprise SaaS platforms operate multi-tenant databases where vendor SREs possess broad diagnostic privileges.

opts.text: Customer Lockbox enforced: Vendor engineers cannot access tenant data without explicit time-limited approval
Standard SaaS operations: Provider manages uptime and internal access under standard security attestations (SOC2)
Uncontrolled / Multi-tenant SaaS with unmonitored vendor telemetry feeds

questions.q: How are encryption keys managed for data at rest across your public cloud and SaaS environments?
questions.hint: If the cloud provider holds or has access to your encryption keys, encryption does NOT defeat foreign subpoenas.

opts.text: Hold Your Own Key (HYOK) / External HSM: Keys generated, stored, and managed in on-prem or sovereign HSMs
Bring Your Own Key (BYOK): Customer imports keys into cloud-managed KMS (provider can access during operations)
Cloud Provider-Managed Keys: Default server-side encryption with provider-owned keys (AWS SSE-S3, Azure PMK)

questions.q: Have you implemented Confidential Computing (hardware-rooted enclaves e.g. AMD SEV-SNP, Intel SGX) for data in use?
questions.hint: Confidential Computing protects data in memory from hypervisor inspection and rogue administrative access.

opts.text: Yes — Deployed in production for high-risk data processing and AI inference
Evaluating / PoC — Testing confidential VMs for regulated financial or healthcare workloads
No — Standard virtualization and container runtimes only

questions.q: Can your organization instantly revoke encryption keys to render foreign-hosted data permanently unreadable?
questions.hint: The definitive technical test of cryptographic sovereignty: remote cryptographic kill-switch.

opts.text: Yes — Cryptographic kill-switch verified: revoking key access instantly blinds all cloud/SaaS data stores
Partial — Can disable keys in cloud console, but cached keys or provider backups may persist
No — Provider manages the lifecycle; instantaneous unilateral revocation is impossible

questions.q: Do you have single-vendor concentration where a disruption to one cloud or SaaS provider halts core business operations?
questions.hint: A primary focus of DORA Art. 28, UK CTP, APRA CPS 230, and MAS Outsourcing guidelines.

opts.text: Severe Concentration: Single hyperscaler / SaaS platform hosts >75% of all critical business functions
Managed Concentration: Dominant primary provider, but critical workloads have documented fallback options
Architectural Multi-Cloud / Hybrid: Workloads portable across distinct providers and on-premises enclaves

questions.q: What is your realistic, tested timeline to execute a complete exit strategy from your primary cloud provider?
questions.hint: Regulatory requirements mandate an actionable, auditable, and tested exit strategy without disruption.

opts.text: Under 3 Months: Workloads are containerized (Kubernetes/OpenShift) and data formats are open standard
6 to 12 Months: Documented transition plan exists, but significant proprietary PaaS rewrites would be required
Over 18 Months / Effectively Impossible: Deep proprietary serverless and database lock-in prevents migration

questions.q: For on-premises hardware, appliances, and telecom equipment, have you audited hardware provenance (e.g. NDAA Section 889)?
questions.hint: National security rules in the US, UK, Australia, and EU ban certain foreign-manufactured telecom and compute components.

opts.text: Fully Audited: Hardware bill of materials (SBOM/HBOM) verified compliant with clean supply chain lists
Partially Audited: Major server vendors certified, but network switches, cameras, and IoT unverified
Not Audited: Hardware procurement driven purely by commercial cost with no origin restrictions
